name: Mid City
description: Mid City is one of Baton Rouge's most eclectic and fast-growing neighborhoods. Known for its murals, local restaurants, and walkable streets, it attracts first-time buyers and investors who want character without the downtown price tag. Craftsman bungalows and renovated shotgun cottages sit alongside new construction infill.
schools: Our Lady of Mercy Catholic School

name: Garden District
description: Baton Rouge's Garden District blends grand historic homes with mature oaks and proximity to LSU and the medical corridor. The neighborhood's tree-canopied streets and classic architecture make it one of the most desirable zip codes in the city, with strong appreciation and low inventory.

name: Zachary
description: Zachary is consistently ranked among Louisiana's top school districts and is a top destination for growing families. Located north of Baton Rouge, it offers larger lots, newer construction, and a strong community identity — all at prices well below the city average.
highlights: #1 rated school district in BR area

name: Prairieville
description: Prairieville has emerged as one of the fastest-growing communities in the Greater Baton Rouge area. Situated in Ascension Parish, it offers spacious new construction homes, top schools, and an easy commute — making it a consistent favorite for move-up buyers.

name: Denham Springs
tagline: Affordable, growing, and close to it all
description: Denham Springs in Livingston Parish offers some of the most affordable home prices in the metro area with strong community growth and new development. Buyers get more space for their dollar — and the city's revitalized antique district has made it a hidden gem.

name: Central
description: Central is a small, incorporated city northeast of Baton Rouge that is fiercely proud of its schools, its tight-knit community, and its quiet suburban lifestyle. It's a top choice for buyers seeking excellent public schools, newer homes, and a true neighborhood feel away from city traffic.

name: Downtown Baton Rouge
tagline: The city's pulse — walkable and vibrant
description: Downtown Baton Rouge is undergoing a major renaissance, with new loft conversions, rooftop bars, and the Shaw Center for the Arts anchoring a growing arts and dining scene. For buyers who want to walk to work, restaurants, and the Mississippi River levee, downtown offers urban living at a value.
schools: Louisiana School for the Visually Impaired

name: Shenandoah
description: Shenandoah is one of Baton Rouge's most established neighborhoods — known for mature trees, well-maintained subdivision lots, and proximity to the Perkins Road corridor. It's a sweet spot for buyers who want a solid home in a proven neighborhood without the premium of the Garden District.
